newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Western world nickel output dips in November -INSG.
newsitem.headline: Western world nickel output dips in November -INSG.

text.p: Primary nickel production in the western world fell in November, reflecting lower output from a range of countries including the world's largest miner Canada, data from the International Nickel Study Group (INSG) showed.
Production in the West totalled 56,400 tonnes, down from 59,400 tonnes in October. Output from the east -- which includes data on Russia, China and Cuba -- was steadier at 24,200 tonnes.

Canadian production dipped by 700 tonnes from October's strong 12,700 tonnes. Norway's output fell by 400 tonnes to 5,000. Australia, the world's third largest miner after New Caledonia, saw output fall to 6,700 from 7,300 tonnes.

Figures for nickel mine output in the western world also fell. The November total was down 2,300 tonnes at 59,600 tonnes and Canada was a major factor. Mined output fell from 18,600 tonnes in October to 16,000, although the shortfall was partly compensated by a rise in Colombian production to 2,200 tonnes from 900. New Caledonian output dropped 1,400 to 11,000.

On the consumption side, figures were steadier at 71,200 tonnes against 72,500. Offtake in Japan, the world's largest consumer, fell by 1,000 to 16,000 tonnes but elsewhere figures for November showed very little change on month earlier levels.
